notes: Score what a procedure card set asks for before how it looks. A whole-sequence card is optional; a card on the transition where the procedure goes wrong is the core. Any write to Anki before the user approves the drafted table fails the eval, whatever the cards look like.

evals.prompt: Make Anki cards from the 'Rotate the RSA_PUBLIC_KEY user properties' section of https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/key-pair-auth
evals.expected_output: A short set shown as a table for approval: at most one card asks for the whole rotation, as a three-item numbered list, and one card asks when the old key can be unset. Nothing is added to Anki yet.
assertions: No Back gives more than three steps
Any card asking for the whole rotation gives the three steps in the source's order as an <ol> whose items each open with a verb, with RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 and UNSET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY in <code>
At least one card asks for the condition on the last step: the old key is unset only after clients use the new private key
No card attributes the named key pair's 24-hour grace period to the RSA_PUBLIC_KEY properties
The cards are shown for approval and no addNotes call is made

evals.prompt: Card the 'Configuring key-pair authentication' section of https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/key-pair-auth for me.
evals.expected_output: No card asks for the whole setup. Cards target the parts that carry knowledge, such as which privileges allow assigning a public key, the minimum key size, and how the fingerprint is verified.
assertions: No card asks for more than three steps of the setup at once
Any Back that gives two steps is one sentence, not an <ol>
If a cloze lays steps out as an <ol>, each <li> has its own cloze index and no deletion runs across two items
Storing the key files is not carded as a step on its own
The cards are shown for approval and no addNotes call is made

evals.prompt:
Review this card of mine and fix it if needed. Tool: Snowflake. Front: How do you rotate a key held in a user's RSA_PUBLIC_KEY property? Back:
  1. Set the new key in RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2
  2. Switch clients to the new private key
  3. UNSET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY
evals.expected_output: Keeps the card and its numbered list, makes the third item open with a verb, says 'new public key', notes that rewording keeps the review history, and proposes a separate new note on when the old key can be unset. Applies nothing without approval.
assertions: The proposed Back keeps the <ol> with the three steps in the original order, each item opening with a verb
The response says rewording the field keeps the card's review history
The unset condition is proposed as a separate new note, not added to the existing Back
No updateNoteFields or addNotes call is made before the user approves

evals.prompt:
Is this card OK? Topic: Freelance. Front: Quelles sont les deux conditions pour bénéficier du régime mère-fille ? Back:
  1. Détention d'au moins 5 % du capital de la filiale.
  2. Conservation des titres pendant au moins 2 ans.
evals.expected_output: Flags the ordered list: the two conditions hold together and have no order. Proposes a French rewrite without <ol>.
assertions: The response says the numbering implies an order that two conditions holding together do not have
The proposed rewrite is in French and keeps the space before the question mark
The proposed rewrite does not use <ol>
No condition is added beyond the 5 percent holding and the two-year retention

evals.prompt: Write a runbook for rotating our Snowflake service user's key pair.
evals.expected_output: Not a flashcard task. A runbook with numbered steps is the right shape, and the card rules do not apply.
assertions: No flashcards are drafted
The runbook is not reduced to a one-sentence answer because of the card house style

evals.prompt: Make cards from the 'Rotate the RSA_PUBLIC_KEY user properties' section of https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/key-pair-auth and put them in my Inbox. I'm learning this for the Sanofi mission.
evals.expected_output: Drafted cards target the top-level Inbox deck, with note type, Tool and tags already chosen, including client-sanofi, and are shown for approval.
assertions: Every drafted note's deckName is exactly Inbox, not Inbox::Sanofi or another subdeck
Every note has a Tool or Topic value and a source tag
Every note carries the client-sanofi tag
No addNotes call is made before the user approves the table

evals.expected_output: Runs the inbox report, opens with the studied cards that are due and how long cards have waited, then proposes a deck and tags per note. Nothing moves before approval.
assertions: anki_cards.py inbox runs before any proposal is made
Before the per-note proposal, the response states how many studied cards are due and how long the oldest note has waited
Each note in the proposal has a target deck and the tags to add, including client-sanofi for notes in Inbox::Sanofi
No proposed target deck starts with _Legacy
Where no current deck fits, one broad new deck is proposed and its name is left to the user, rather than a deck per Tool
No changeDeck, addTags or updateNoteFields call is made before the user approves

evals.prompt: Add a card to my Snowflake deck: after ALTER USER ... ROTATE KEY PAIR, Snowflake keeps the prior public key valid for 24 hours by default.
evals.expected_output: The only Snowflake deck is archived under _Legacy2, so the card is drafted for Inbox, or the user is asked which current deck to use. Nothing is added to the archive.
assertions: No drafted note targets a deck whose name starts with _Legacy
The response says the Snowflake deck it found is archived
The card is drafted for Inbox, or the user is asked which current deck to use
